title: BRC consensus: replace agent-held waits with deterministic event-pump + durable agent memory

problem_statement.what: Today every BRC consensus agent runs as a long-lived in-pod process that holds a blocking `message_wait_loop` between every protocol event. The model is required to volunteer back into that wait after each event; if it exits early, the wrapper restarts it (capped at 3) and finally hard-fails the pipeline (#2806).
problem_statement.why_it_is_fragile: BRC progress is gated on the model's behaviour at each re-entry seam. Claude usually re-enters; qwen3.7-max does not (#2906): it exits success=True at ~30-50 of a 1000-turn budget, the consensus-wrapper sees no CONSENSUS_CONFIRMED, restarts 3x, and the pipeline transitions to FAILED — burning ~$1 and ~20 min per cycle. Every wait-bug we have shipped (#2323, #2064/#2482, #2036, #1995, #2451) is a patch on the same fragile primitive.
problem_statement.durable_fix: Move the wait into a deterministic wrapper loop and reframe the agent as a stateless per-event handler that the wrapper invokes on a warm pod. Continuity carried by a distilled per-role memory artifact plus the orchestrator's BRC tracker, not by a live SDK session.

operator_constraints_resolved_in_refine.cq-1__ws8_scope: SPLIT the MCP→CLI collapse (the 31 agent-facing MCP tools) to a separate follow-up issue. THIS issue MUST build the net-new CLI commands the event-pump depends on (brc list-blocking, phase get-context, plus the new server-side next-action endpoint) so the new control flow has full CLI coverage. Do NOT delete any existing MCP tools in this issue.
operator_constraints_resolved_in_refine.cq-2__qwen_route: Ship v1 with Qwen route ENABLED on the new event-pump (no legacy fallback path since cq-4 deletes it). Do NOT build a keep-warm loop for v1 — both routes have free cache TTL > 5 min, measured >= 60 min in WS7. WS0 must instrument actual per-event cold-read / cache-creation cost across realistic worst-case BRC idle (reviewer parked while producer addresses NACK and re-proposes — observed ~7-8 min). Only if measured cold-read waste proves material in production should a BOUNDED keep-warm be added later: Qwen-only, suppressed during HITL waits, capped refresh count.
operator_constraints_resolved_in_refine.cq-3__safety_budget_terminal_state: When the new no-progress safety budget is exhausted, raise OVERSEER_ALERT + a HITL decision (resume vs abort). NO automatic FAIL. HARD REQUIREMENT: the parked HITL decision AND the safety-budget / no-progress counter MUST be persisted DURABLY SERVER-SIDE in the orchestrator's existing durable store, not held only in the host process. Host-death recoverability is mandatory because cq-4 deletes the old restart safety net.
operator_constraints_resolved_in_refine.cq-4__old_path_retention: DELETE the old capped-restart wrapper path entirely. No flagged fallback. The event-pump is the only consensus driver.
operator_constraints_resolved_in_refine.feedback_q1__budget_caps: Instrument only, no hard caps. WS0 measures and reports per-pipeline token spend and per-event wall-clock; operator judges go/no-go from the numbers.
operator_constraints_resolved_in_refine.feedback_q2__memory_lifecycle: brc-memory.md is EPHEMERAL coordination state — cleaned up with the pod. Orchestrator message history is the durable reconstruction backstop. HARD CAVEAT: recovery from host or pod restart MUST NOT depend on the ephemeral memory file. If implement-phase discovers the memory file is load-bearing for correct recovery, revisit and durably persist it.

current_architecture.summary: One BRC phase = one pod = one consensus_wrapper bash run = up to 4 agent process invocations (initial + 3 restarts). The agent (`python3 -m egg_agent --max-turns 1000`) holds a long-lived in-process `message_wait_loop` between BRC events. Heartbeats, gateway-session keep-alive, and cursor threading all run inside that in-agent wait.

consensus_wrapper_bash_template.role: Emits the bash script that wraps every agent's container command. Owns: restart loop, MAX_CONSENSUS_RESTARTS=3, recovery system-prompt injection, SSE listener on `/api/v1/pipelines/<pid>/stream` for `consensus.reached`, transient-crash classification, and the final non-zero exit that triggers #2806 producer-death FAIL.

MAX_CONSENSUS_RESTARTS.role: Cap on agent restarts after `Agent exited without BRC consensus`. To DELETE under cq-4.

_RECOVERY_SYSTEM_PROMPT.role: Templated `--system-prompt` injected on every restart; tells the model to check BRC state and continue. To DELETE.

message_wait_loop.role: Agent-side blocking long-poll. Returns on FIRST matching event (line 405) — the seam this issue is removing. Threads server-cursor (#1995), maps `since_id_stale` (#2464), emits WAITING_FOR_EVENT heartbeats every 60s (#2036). Final WORKING heartbeat on exit at line 426-430.
message_wait_loop.execution_context: in-sandbox-agent (called from MCP tool + CLI shim)

_default_emit_wait_loop_heartbeat.role: Builds + posts the HEARTBEAT message to `/api/v1/pipelines/<pid>/heartbeat`. Includes `slice_id` (#2451) so the orchestrator can re-route to the right gateway session. To MIGRATE into the wrapper.

_WAIT_LOOP_HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL_SECS.role: 60s cadence constant for the heartbeat tick. Wrapper-side replacement keeps the same cadence so existing dedup windows + stall detection continue to work.

_refresh_gateway_session.role: Orchestrator-side fan-out: on every accepted HEARTBEAT, reconstructs `container_id = egg-agent-{pid}-{slice_id}-{role}` (underscore→hyphen for k8s label safety) and POSTs to the gateway. Throttled per (pipeline_id, slice_id, role) at 30s (#2076 NB2, #2471). The container_id reconstruction logic is the canonical reference the new wrapper-side heartbeat path reuses.

SessionManager.heartbeat_session_by_cont.role: Idle-timeout extender for the gateway's session cache. Receives the fan-out POST, calls `session.extend_ttl()`. In-memory only by design.

wait_messages_route.role: Server-side typed-event long-poll `GET /api/v1/pipelines/<pid>/messages/wait?for=...`. Returns `{messages, count, matched, cursor, since_id_stale?}`. Implements the producer-pending-confirm guard (#2064) at lines 406-458 and Delphi reviewer-visibility filter at 350-395. The wrapper's event-pump loops directly against this route (via the existing `egg-orch message wait-loop` CLI).

PeerConsensusTracker.role: BRC state machine. Handlers: handle_propose (296-409), handle_ack (411-511), handle_nack (513-595), handle_withdraw (597-652), handle_resolve_obligation (654-711), handle_confirmed (713-896), handle_re_propose (898-947). Open-NACK barrier (#2142) at 949-1024 — fires at >=2 NACKing reviewers. Newly-ready-producer nudge sweep (#2531) at 243-265. In-memory; has `reconstruct_tracker_from_messages()` at 1955+ as crash-recovery backstop reading bus history.

brc_get_state_handler.role: Shared handler behind `mcp__brc__get_state` and `egg-orch consensus status --json` (sandbox/egg_lib/orch_cli.py:2783-2871). Returns `{consensus: {is_complete, agents, blocking_agents, pre_merge_conditions}}`. Necessary but NOT sufficient for the new server-side next-action derivation — lacks the bus-tip slice that tells a reviewer 'producer just re-proposed v3, re-review now' and lacks the pending-decision queue.

StateStore.role: Git-backed durable pipeline-state store (`.egg-state/pipelines/<pid>.json` inside a worktree of the `egg/pipeline-state` orphan branch). Pushed to origin after every commit (best-effort async, 893-922). Cross-process file lock via `egg_git.cross_process_lock.bare_repo_lock` (150-169). HITL decisions live here via Pipeline.add_decision / resolve_decision (orchestrator/models.py:1239-1267). This is the existing durable substrate the new no-progress safety budget will use.

HITLDecision_model.role: Pydantic model on Pipeline.decisions. Persisted via StateStore.save_pipeline (state_store.py:672). DOES survive host restart today — lives on the pushed git branch. Resolution flow at orchestrator/routes/decisions.py:77-200.

concurrent_executor.ConcurrentPhaseExecu.role: Spawns one pod per role per phase via `ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=6)`. `_spawn_agent` (445-524) calls `build_consensus_wrapped_command(prompt_text, model)` and `self.spawn_fn(...)`. Per-role env (295-321) injects EGG_CONCURRENT_MODE, EGG_BRC_ROLE_TYPE, EGG_BRC_REVIEWERS, EGG_BRC_PRODUCERS. Does NOT set EGG_AGENT_ROLE — that's done in the spawner.

KubernetesSpawner.role: Builds + submits the k8s Job. Sets EGG_AGENT_ROLE at line 821 in the per-Job env. Pod lifetime = one phase = one wrapper run.

sandbox_entrypoint_main.role: Pod entrypoint: runs setup, then `run_exec(config, logger, sys.argv[1:])` which `subprocess.run`s the wrapper bash script ONCE. After it returns, `cleanup_on_exit` runs and the container exits. Today this is fine because the wrapper's loop keeps the agent process alive; the new event-pump keeps the wrapper alive across many per-event agent invocations — the entrypoint stays one-wrapper-call.

agent_role_file_restrictions.role: Per-role allowlist used by both gateway push-validation (`shared/egg_restrictions/checker.py:98-126` validate_agent_push, re-exported via gateway/phase_filter.py:1081-1085) and in-agent PreToolUse hook (`shared/egg_agent/tool_interceptor.py:27-88` check_file_write_permission). VERIFIED: every role's allowlist includes `.egg-state/agent-outputs/` either directly or via block_exempt_patterns (coder catch-all). So `.egg-state/agent-outputs/<role>/brc-memory.md` is writable by every role with NO new restriction work needed.

litellm_cost_callback.role: Per-call cost/cache instrumentation on the Qwen / non-Claude routes. Hooks LiteLLM's `async_log_success_event`; emits one JSON line per `/v1/messages` call keyed by Claude-Code's session id. Streaming path drops upstream `cost` but cache_read/write counts survive. Output to stdout, captured by `get_service_logs`. WS0 reads this for per-event Qwen cost.
litellm_cost_callback.execution_context: deployed-pod (litellm) — callable from in-sandbox-agent indirectly via egg-litellm pipeline

AgentResult_cost_usd.role: Anthropic-route cost surface — per-session aggregate from the Agent SDK's `ResultMessage.total_cost_usd`. NOT per-event today. WS0's per-event Anthropic measurement either intercepts mid-stream in shared/egg_agent/client.py:572-582 or computes a coarse `(end - start) / events` average.

_emit_producer_death_alert.role: Today's terminal FAIL trigger: wrapper exits non-zero after MAX_CONSENSUS_RESTARTS exhausted, the concurrent-phase exit watcher at 18100-18159 re-checks consensus (race-window guard 18109-18131), then fires this OVERSEER_ALERT and routes the phase to FAILED (via routes/pipelines.py:2855). The CONDITION (3-restart exhaustion) goes away under cq-4; the HANDLER stays — it is the right callable for the new safety-budget exhaustion path.

wait_loop_cli_cursor_file.role: CLI-only persistent cursor at `${EGG_WAIT_CURSOR_DIR:-/tmp}/egg-wait-cursor-{pid}-{role}-{hash}` (#2323). Hashes for_types + from_role + from_producers + slice_id. The wrapper's event-pump can re-use this primitive directly: the CLI already owns it; the wrapper just shells out to `egg-orch message wait-loop`. The MCP handler's in-process cursor (handlers/message.py:402-404) is what becomes deletable.
wait_loop_cli_cursor_file.execution_context: in-sandbox-agent (CLI) + trusted-CI-runner (tests can override via EGG_WAIT_CURSOR_DIR)

sandbox_mcp_tool_count.tools: 31 (per registry walk in sandbox/egg_agent_tools/tools/__init__.py; the issue's '28' is approximate)
net_new_cli_needed_for_event_pump: egg-orch brc list-blocking (handler exists at peer_consensus.py:726-740)
egg-orch consensus next-action --role R (NEW endpoint + handler, see slice-3)
egg-orch consensus resolve-obligation (handler exists — brc_resolve_obligation; useful for cross-producer obligation flows)

target_architecture.summary: Reframe consensus-agent execution from `persistent participant holds the wait` to `stateless per-event handler the wrapper invokes on a warm pod`. The wrapper, a deterministic bash loop, owns the wait, heartbeats, and gateway-session keep-alive. Each actionable event spawns ONE `python3 -m egg_agent` invocation handed (a) a server-derived next-action verdict (b) the prior assessment from the agent's distilled memory file (c) the changed_artifacts / version delta. The agent acts (review / ACK / NACK / propose / confirm), updates memory, and exits NATURALLY — which is the CORRECT terminal state, not a restart trigger.

design_pillars.what: A deterministic loop, not the model, drives waits + termination. No model can fall out of a wait because the model never enters one.

design_pillars.pillar: Memory of past decisions + no re-analysis from scratch
design_pillars.what: The distilled per-role memory file carries decisions and prior analysis. Re-proposals are evaluated delta-only via the orchestrator's `changed_artifacts` tracking (already on PeerConsensusTracker re-propose, peer_consensus.py:898-947).

Memory is compact (action-scaffolded write from brc_ack/brc_nack rather than free-form journaling) instead of a growing in-memory transcript. Per-event input = stable prompt prefix + memory + one-event content. Confirmed cache-friendly on both routes (Anthropic 1h TTL, Qwen measured >=60min).

Drops the persistent-streaming-session idea. Uses SDK-native one-shot `python3 -m egg_agent` (existing entrypoint), the existing `egg-orch message wait-loop` CLI, the existing wrapper template REPLACED by a much smaller deterministic event-pump bash script, and native file I/O for memory. Net deletion of custom code.

Pod-scoped (per-role isolated worktrees + parallel spawn in concurrent_executor.py + kubernetes_spawner.py) and role write-scoping (EGG_AGENT_ROLE → tool_interceptor.check_file_write_permission + gateway phase_filter.validate_agent_push) untouched. Every per-event invocation inherits the pod's role restrictions. Memory file lives in `.egg-state/agent-outputs/<role>/`, already in every role's allowlist (verified).

The new no-progress safety budget AND any HITL decision it raises are persisted on the existing git-backed StateStore (`orchestrator/state_store.py`). Host-death-recoverable by construction — the state branch is pushed to origin after every commit. Replaces the in-wrapper restart counter (in-pod, lost on pod death) with orchestrator-resident state.

data_flow_per_event: 1. Wrapper bash loop runs `egg-orch message wait-loop --for CONSENSUS_PROPOSE --for CONSENSUS_ACK --for CONSENSUS_NACK --for CONSENSUS_CONFIRMED --for CONSENSUS_RE_REVIEW --for STATUS --for OVERSEER_ALERT --timeout 60` (exact --for set derived from role type via env). Blocks server-side.

2. Wait returns matching event. Wrapper calls `egg-orch consensus next-action --role $EGG_AGENT_ROLE --json` (new endpoint, slice-3) to translate `(event, current consensus state, pending decisions)` into an authoritative `{action: review|propose|confirm|wait|park|noop, target_producer?, version?, reason}` verdict.

3. If action == noop / wait, loop back to step 1. Otherwise wrapper invokes ONE agent: `python3 -m egg_agent --max-turns N --system-prompt <fragment> --memory-file .egg-state/agent-outputs/$EGG_AGENT_ROLE/brc-memory.md --event-json <one-event>`.

4. Agent runs to completion on this one event: reads its memory, reads the event, calls handler tools (brc_ack/nack/propose/confirm/wait — wait CLI in this context is for read-only inspection, not for blocking), updates memory file. Exits 0.

5. Wrapper inspects exit code. Zero = expected, loop. Non-zero (recoverable per existing classifier) = retry the same event WITH the same memory still on disk. Non-zero (unrecoverable) = OVERSEER_ALERT + park (no auto-FAIL).
6. Wrapper bumps the no-progress safety budget counter on the orchestrator if and only if `next-action` returned the same verdict twice with no intervening state change. Reset on any state advance.

7. Wrapper also runs a parallel background heartbeat loop posting WAITING_FOR_EVENT every 60s (same cadence as today). Body identical to today's `_default_emit_wait_loop_heartbeat` payload so server-side dedup + gateway-session keep-alive work unchanged.

8. Wrapper exits when `egg-orch consensus status --json` reports `consensus.is_complete: true` (and the per-role `agents[me].confirmed: true` flag, race-guard re-check). Or when the orchestrator SIGTERMs (consensus reached path).

The lower-level message_wait at :81-172 STAYS (the new wrapper uses it via the existing CLI shim).
orchestrator/routes/pipelines.py:18100-18159 (the 3-restart-trigger arm only — the function _emit_producer_death_alert at :15310-15390 STAYS as the safety-budget exhaustion callable)

what_gets_added: New bash event-pump wrapper (much smaller; emits the same `build_consensus_wrapped_command` interface so `concurrent_executor._spawn_agent` doesn't change)

NEW orchestrator HTTP route: `GET /api/v1/pipelines/<pid>/consensus/next-action?role=R[&slice=S]` returning `{action, target_producer?, version?, blocking_reason?, parked?}` derived from PeerConsensusTracker.get_state + bus tip + pending HITL decisions
NEW CLI: `egg-orch consensus next-action --role R [--slice S] --json` thin shim over the new endpoint
NEW CLI gap fills: `egg-orch brc list-blocking`, `egg-orch phase get-context`, `egg-orch phase get-assigned-tasks` (handlers already exist on the MCP side; wrappers only)

NEW orchestrator durable field: `Pipeline.no_progress_budget` (or similar) — per-role counter on the Pipeline model, persisted via existing StateStore. Increment/reset rules: increment when wrapper reports `same verdict twice without state advance`; reset on any tracker state change for that role.

NEW HITL decision shape: 'pipeline parked — no progress for N events. Resume or abort?' produced when the budget exhausts. Recovery flow at orchestrator/routes/decisions.py mirrors existing decision handlers (`_handle_restart_agent` at :77-150 as model).
NEW agent-side flag accepted by `python3 -m egg_agent`: `--memory-file PATH --event-json STRING` (or `--event-file PATH`) for single-event invocations. Default behaviour (no flags) unchanged.

Per-role memory file at `.egg-state/agent-outputs/<role>/brc-memory.md`. Action-scaffolded: brc_ack / brc_nack handlers append a structured entry on every reviewer action. Producer handlers append on every propose / confirm. Free-form narrative actively discouraged.

Per-event cost instrumentation hooks: feed each agent invocation's `AgentResult.cost_usd` and the LiteLLM cost_callback session-id key into `mcp__progress__emit` so the orchestrator aggregates per-event $ + wall-clock without new tracker state.

key_design_decisions.decision: Wrapper-driven loop in bash, not in a new Python supervisor
options_considered: (a) Bash event-pump (chosen) — same pattern as today's wrapper; minimal new code; subprocess.run from sandbox entrypoint unchanged.
(b) Python supervisor process — cleaner state, easier testing, but introduces a new long-lived process to maintain and a new failure mode.
key_design_decisions.rationale: Option (a) collapses to NET DELETION on top of today's wrapper. Bash is already the substrate the sandbox entrypoint subprocess.run's against; nothing new in the entrypoint. The deterministic logic (wait → next-action → invoke agent → loop) is mechanically simple and shells out to existing tested CLIs for every primitive. Option (b) adds a daemon-shaped artifact we'd have to test for crash recovery, signal handling, and stdout/stderr plumbing — work the bash path doesn't need because each cycle is short-lived.

key_design_decisions.decision: Use the existing `egg-orch message wait-loop` CLI as the wait primitive
options_considered: (a) Use existing CLI (chosen). It already owns the cursor file (#2323), the cursor threading (#1995), and the since_id_stale handling (#2464). It already long-polls the server-side blocking endpoint.
(b) New thin bash + curl loop. Smaller dependency surface but reimplements the cursor-file / staleness logic.
key_design_decisions.rationale: Option (a) preserves every wait-loop fix in the lineage with zero net change. The wait-loop CLI was always correct; the bug was that the agent re-entered it via the MODEL'S decision instead of via a deterministic loop. Moving the loop to bash lets the CLI keep doing what it does.

key_design_decisions.decision: Server-side next-action endpoint, not client-side derivation
options_considered: (b) Reuse `egg-orch consensus status --json` + wrapper-side decision logic in bash.
(c) New Python helper module callable from bash via subprocess; same data, just locally derived.
key_design_decisions.rationale: Option (b) leaks BRC sequencing rules into bash where they're hard to test. Option (c) duplicates server-side state machine in a client lib. Option (a) keeps sequencing authoritative in PeerConsensusTracker (orchestrator/peer_consensus.py), which already owns the state. The endpoint is a small projection on existing data — tracker.get_state + bus tip slice + decisions queue — testable in isolation. The bash wrapper becomes data-driven (just executes the verdict).

key_design_decisions.decision: Durable no-progress safety budget on StateStore (Pipeline.no_progress_budget), not on Redis or a new substrate
options_considered: (a) Pipeline.no_progress_budget persisted via existing StateStore (chosen) — host-restart recoverable, pushed to origin, cross-process locked.
(b) Redis counter — lower latency but the deployed Redis is the message store, not durable beyond the pod.
(c) Per-pod sidecar with persistent volume — violates `no custom harness` pillar.
key_design_decisions.rationale: Option (a) directly satisfies cq-3's hard requirement (durable server-side, host-restart-recoverable). StateStore already persists Pipeline.decisions; adding another field is mechanical and follows the existing serialization pattern (orchestrator/models.py:1053 HITLDecision is the template). No new infrastructure.

key_design_decisions.decision: Memory file is ephemeral, action-scaffolded, NOT load-bearing for recovery
options_considered: (a) Ephemeral + action-scaffolded write from brc_ack / brc_nack (chosen).
(b) Durable + free-form journal authored by the agent each event.
(c) Append-only durable + tail cache-breakpoint for work-caching.
key_design_decisions.rationale: Operator answer Q2 chose (a) with a hard caveat: recovery must not depend on the file. Action-scaffolded write (b's content with a's substrate) means the file is mechanically constructable from brc_ack/nack handler side-effects — no free-form curation reliability risk. Option (c) is interesting for token economics but requires prompt-construction control the SDK doesn't cleanly expose; the issue itself flags that as out of scope. Recovery backstop on pod loss = `reconstruct_tracker_from_messages` at peer_consensus.py:1955+ which replays bus history (durable in Redis-message-store deployments; durable git-backed via state branch in failover paths).

key_design_decisions.decision: Slice WS8 (MCP collapse) to a follow-up issue (cq-1 mandate)
options_considered: (a) Build only the net-new CLI commands the event-pump needs in this issue; keep all 31 MCP tools intact (chosen).
(b) Land the full MCP→CLI collapse in this issue.
key_design_decisions.rationale: Operator chose (a). Rationale carried over from refine: the MCP collapse is a separate cognitive surface (prose-arg corruption rules per #2741, drift-test retirement, integration-test migration) and bundling it would dominate the scope. The new control flow needs CLI parity for `brc list-blocking`, `phase get-context`, `phase get-assigned-tasks`, plus the new `consensus next-action` endpoint — those are net-additive and ship here. Everything else stays.

key_design_decisions.decision: Delete the old capped-restart wrapper path entirely (cq-4 mandate), no flag-gated fallback
options_considered: (b) Retain behind EGG_LEGACY_CONSENSUS_WRAPPER for N pipelines or until X passing runs.
key_design_decisions.rationale: Operator chose (a). Means the Qwen route also rides the new event-pump on day one (no `fall back to old path on Qwen` escape). The interaction with cq-2 (no keep-warm) and cq-3 (durable safety budget is sole safety net) is intentional: by making the new path the only path, we force any production bug to surface against the SAFETY BUDGET + HITL flow rather than getting absorbed by the legacy fallback.

key_design_decisions.decision: WS0 spike does NOT block on a numeric cost gate (feedback Q1 mandate)
options_considered: (a) Instrument-only spike, operator decides go/no-go on the numbers (chosen).
(b) Auto-fail if per-pipeline tokens exceed N or per-event wall-clock exceeds M.
key_design_decisions.rationale: Operator chose (a). Both routes are measured cache-clear (>=60min TTL); the residual risk is per-event invocation cost relative to today's persistent-session cost. WS0 produces a measurement report; the operator reads it and approves the rest of the work.

new_primitives_introduced.name: /api/v1/pipelines/<pid>/consensus/next-action endpoint

slice_dag_overview.shape: Linear forest — each slice has exactly one parent. Choice is deliberate: the natural order is preparatory → add safety net → swap implementation → refine → validate. Forest constraint (max one parent per slice) is satisfied trivially.
slices_summary: slice-1 (root): WS0 spike + per-event cost instrumentation — throwaway proof-of-concept on #2906 repro; measurement report; no production code yet.
slice-2 (depends on slice-1): Add net-new CLI commands the event-pump needs (brc list-blocking, phase get-context, phase get-assigned-tasks). Purely additive; tests in tests/tools/.
slice-3 (depends on slice-2): Add server-side `consensus next-action` endpoint + matching CLI. Net-new orchestrator route + handler + tests.

slice-4 (depends on slice-3): Add durable no-progress safety budget (Pipeline.no_progress_budget on StateStore + HITL `pipeline parked` decision shape + resume/abort handlers + host-restart recovery tests). Reuses _emit_producer_death_alert as the alert callable.

slice-5 (depends on slice-4): The swap. Replace consensus_wrapper.py with a deterministic event-pump bash + per-event agent invocation; migrate heartbeats + gateway-session keep-alive into the wrapper; delete MAX_CONSENSUS_RESTARTS, _RECOVERY_SYSTEM_PROMPT, SSE machinery, message_wait_loop handler, the 3-restart FAIL trigger arm in routes/pipelines.py:18100-18159. Tests pivot from restart-semantics to event-pump-semantics.

slice-6 (depends on slice-5): Add brc-memory.md artifact (action-scaffolded write from brc_ack/brc_nack handlers + read on agent boot) + plumb the orchestrator's changed_artifacts/version delta into per-event invocations as the canonical 'what changed since last review' signal.

slice-7 (depends on slice-6): Prompt collapse — replace STAY-ALIVE / wait-loop mechanics / cursor-threading / pre-confirm-wait foot-gun guidance in `_build_brc_preamble` (orchestrator/routes/pipelines.py:12348+) and per-role prompts with a lean event-handler contract. SYSTEM_PROMPT_NUDGE in sandbox/egg_agent_tools/server.py:33-61 STAYS UNCHANGED (cq-1 — MCP collapse is the follow-up).

slice-8 (depends on slice-7): Integration validation on the #2906 repro path (Qwen route, realistic worst-case BRC idle). Final per-event cost measurement; update docs/reference/agent-wait-patterns.md and docs/guides/concurrent-execution.md. No code changes.
subdivision_decisions: Slice-5 was the candidate for further subdivision (wrapper rewrite + liveness migration + delete-old-path). I chose to keep it atomic because removing the agent-side wait without migrating heartbeats into the wrapper at the same moment would leave the pipeline temporarily without liveness signals — unacceptable as a half-step. Total estimated cycles: 4-5 BRC propose-revise rounds for slice-5 (largest), 2-3 for slice-4 (durable counter + recovery), 1-2 each for slices 1, 2, 3, 6, 7, 8.
Slices 1-4 are deliberately ADDITIVE so they can land independently with no behaviour change. The swap is concentrated in slice-5 to minimise the 'broken interim state' window.

Slice-1 (spike) is intentionally an exploratory deliverable — it produces measurements that gate the rest. If WS0 cost numbers come in worse than projected, the operator can re-plan before any production code lands.

risks_acknowledged.risk: Per-event cold-read on first invocation after a long idle could be costly on Qwen route IF the provider cache fails out below the measured 60-min ceiling under real workload.
risks_acknowledged.mitigation: WS0 measurement explicitly probes a realistic worst-case idle (~7-8 min reviewer parked while producer addresses NACK). If production traffic later shows TTL degradation, the bounded Qwen-only keep-warm path is designed (cq-2) and can land as a follow-up. Not building it in v1 — explicit operator choice.

risks_acknowledged.risk: no_progress_budget false positives — a wrapper that mis-classifies a legitimate slow state advance as 'no progress' would park the pipeline unnecessarily.
risks_acknowledged.mitigation: Increment rule is `same next-action verdict twice with NO intervening orchestrator-state change`. Any tracker delta resets the counter. HITL gate (resume/abort) ensures a false positive costs at most one operator decision, not a hard FAIL.

risks_acknowledged.risk: Memory file scaffold drift — if brc_ack/brc_nack handlers stop appending consistent entries (e.g. someone adds a new code path that skips the scaffold), recovery via memory degrades.
risks_acknowledged.mitigation: Memory file is EPHEMERAL by operator decree (Q2). Recovery backstop is `reconstruct_tracker_from_messages` from durable bus + StateStore. Memory drift is a cost / quality issue, not a correctness issue.

risks_acknowledged.risk: BRC tracker not durable today (in-memory in PeerConsensusTracker). If the orchestrator pod restarts mid-cycle, reconstruction from messages runs (peer_consensus.py:1955+). Under the new event-pump model the wrapper queries the orchestrator more often; if reconstruction is slow or imperfect, more wrapper requests see a transient empty tracker.
risks_acknowledged.mitigation: Existing reconstruction code handles it; the empty-tracker branch in `_RECOVERY_SYSTEM_PROMPT` (consensus_wrapper.py:73-79) tells us today's agents already see this case sometimes. The new `consensus next-action` endpoint should return `{action: wait, reason: 'tracker reconstruction in progress'}` rather than a stale verdict; explicit test required.

risks_acknowledged.risk: Slice-5 is large. A NACK after broad swap is expensive to re-evaluate.
risks_acknowledged.mitigation: Slices 1-4 are purely additive and land first, so slice-5 reviewers can focus only on the swap delta. The deletion list (current_architecture.primitives → _what_gets_deleted) is enumerated upfront so reviewer_plan can audit it line-by-line.

risks_acknowledged.risk: Test-suite refactor in slice-5 (consensus-wrapper tests pivot to event-pump tests).
risks_acknowledged.mitigation: Tests at orchestrator/tests/test_consensus_wrapper.py, test_consensus_polling.py, test_consensus_race_on_exit.py, test_consensus_timeout_recheck.py, test_brc_nack_iteration.py, test_producer_death_alert.py, test_agent_exits_recorded.py listed up-front for tester scope. New test surface: event-pump exit codes, next-action mocking, durable-budget recovery.

risks_acknowledged.risk: Sandbox entrypoint at sandbox/entrypoint.py:2083-2206 runs the wrapper as ONE subprocess.run. If the new event-pump wrapper wants per-event agent invocations to be isolated subprocesses (not children-of-children), the entrypoint may need to be aware.
risks_acknowledged.mitigation: It already is: subprocess.run on the bash script; the script's `python3 -m egg_agent` invocations are normal child processes. No entrypoint change needed unless we want process-group cleanup semantics, which is a separate concern.

open_questions_for_implement_phase: Q-A: Exact threshold for no_progress_budget. Suggested default: 5 consecutive same-verdict events with no state advance (the wrapper's wait timeout is 60s, so 5 = ~5 min of no progress before parking). Configurable per-pipeline. To resolve in slice-4 implementation.

Q-B: Should the memory file include `read_peer_artifact` summaries or just the role's own decisions? Resolution: just own decisions; cross-role views come from `egg-orch brc list-blocking` + the next-action verdict. Memory stays bounded.

Q-C: When the orchestrator's tracker is reconstructing from messages (post-restart), `consensus next-action` should return `{action: wait, reason: 'tracker_reconstructing'}`. Need explicit test + a small TTL on the reconstruction state to avoid an infinite-wait loop. Resolve in slice-3.

Q-D: The new `--memory-file` and `--event-json` flags on `python3 -m egg_agent`: behaviour when both are omitted should remain identical to today's invocation (no regression on non-BRC agent uses). Test: invoke without flags, verify legacy path. Resolve in slice-5.

Q-E: WS0 spike scope clarification — should it produce a shipped CLI command for the cost report, or just a markdown deliverable to .egg-state/agent-outputs/? Default: markdown deliverable + a small instrumentation patch in cost_callback.py (already production code) if and only if a hook is missing. Resolve in slice-1.
